quest.title: Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights
quest.description: A sudden accident occurs at the scene of the magic show, and the chosen audience member is also nowhere to be found. All indications point to Lyney and Lynette, but you have your doubts...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1425, Primogem x30, Mora x62225, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, Officer. How's the investigation going?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're Lyney and Lynette's attorneys.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. You must be the traveler that Lady Furina mentioned. Listen, I'll be perfectly honest with you... I'd avoid getting mixed up in this whirlpool of a mess if I were you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Come with me and you'll see.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: The deceased is one of Lyney's assistants, named Cowell. Even though he hadn't joined the troupe long, he was hardworking and everyone generally liked him.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: The assistants are usually in charge of setting up and inspecting the props, as well as assisting with the show and keeping the crowd engaged.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: As you probably saw when you were in the audience, the water tank suddenly fell and smashed the box with Cowell inside it.

choices.text: But why was Cowell inside?

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: This is the real mystery. We've already searched the scene and were unable to find any traces of the girl.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: However, if you look carefully, the box was positioned directly under the water tank. The ropes holding the tank were then burned by the pyrotechnics on stage, causing them to snap.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: All these factors lining up so perfectly makes it hard to see this as a mere accident.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: If anything, the more logical explanation is that the whole incident was intentionally planned, and Lyney is the most likely person to have access to all these areas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he doesn't have a motive...

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: Are you both good friends of his?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, well, you can't say we're "good friends," but we've known each other for, uh, a little while.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: So in just a short time, he was not only able to win your trust, but even convince you to act as his attorneys.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: I know there's no such thing as "magic." The real trick of a magician is holding the audience in the palm of their hand.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: I've seen a lot of cases, and I can tell you that people are the least reliable kind of evidence.

choices.text: But that's not always true.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: Sorry, I tend to be pretty straightforward... Just know that I'm warning you for your own good.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: Anyway, you may investigate the scene of the crime yourselves if you're curious. Who knows, maybe you'll be able to come up with some new evidence.

choices.text: People can also be the most reliable evidence.
Wasn't the girl supposed to be in there?

dialogues.text: Hey, you! Yes, both of you! Over here! I've been keeping an eye on you for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you mean us?
That's right! If I'm not mistaken, you're also among those who wish to cut down the thorns and pursue the truth, no? And by the looks of it, you're not from Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you're right on the Mora about that one... But who are you?
Hehehe, have you never heard of the Spina di Rosula?
From mediating disputes and providing protection, to solving conundrums — you name it, Spina di Rosula does it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And I, Navia, have the honor of being its renowned president...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Though those who play by our rules call me "Boss."

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: I'm Silver, her attendant. Pleased to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: And I'm Melus. Demoiselle's various daily needs and affairs are under my purview.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Boss, Demoiselle... What gives with the names?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ahem... Well, I am the second-generation president. Melus and the others are still used to my... previous title.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: My apologies, Demoiselle. Should you prefer "Boss," I will endeavor to use that instead.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, no need. You don't have to call me Boss, just "Navia" is fine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, if you say so... Not that we're members of Spina di Rosula, anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha, all merely trifling details, never mind. Now, back to the situation at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you want to investigate as well?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's right. I've always kept an eye on the serial disappearance cases — my interest stems from a matter back from my father's time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Judging from the look of things, I find Lyney an unlikely mastermind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? We think so too! That's why we're looking for clues now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how did you come to that conclusion?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Intuition, naturally. My unparalleled intuition!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Furina sure was quick to point the finger at Lyney without any decisive evidence whatsoever, wasn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But that's not uncommon for her. If you remember, the Justice had to interrupt her and ask if she was pressing charges just to keep her from getting carried away.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, a trial begins the moment someone levels charges. And of course, there was no way Furina was going to back down in that situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds more like you just don't trust the Hydro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, what's your opinion? I must admit that she can be interesting at times, but liking her doesn't mean that I'll blindly agree with her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, when you put it like that...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright, I've answered your question. Now it's time you answer mine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, did that answer count?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I say it does. But don't worry! You won't hear any pointless questions from me!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In your opinion, do you think it's right to treat a trial like it's an opera?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not always.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And why would that be?

choices.text: Doing so makes it easy for the truth to fall by the wayside.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha! See, Silver and Melus? I told you they'd be different!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Most astute of you, Demoiselle. I, too, think that the Traveler's response was most excellent.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: No matter how wonderful the script or how fervent the audience's expectations may be, the trials that go on stage here must be based in fact.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: And if that can be done, Boss, then—

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, that's quite enough, Melus. Anyway, I like your answer. You pass with flying colors!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Now, I need to make some preparations, following which our joint investigation shall commence... You two shall be my assistants!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, since when did we become assistants!?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm? Oh. Well, I can be the assistant, sure — or your companion, if you like. I'm really not that fussy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. That's more like it.

choices.text: I think you're missing the point, Paimon...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Far be it from me to brag, but I believe that Demoiselle's intuition will be instrumental in uncovering the truth.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: You wish to save a friend from false accusations, and we wish to unravel the disappearances. In this sense, our goals are aligned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, you have a point. You're quite the talker, aren't you, mister?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what about you over there? What do you think? You seem like you've got something on your mind.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: I have nothing to add.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, alrighty then...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We'll be making some preparations first. Just be sure to let us know if they start revealing Lyney's tricks. Thanks!

choices.text: Seems you've already agreed, then.
Something serious like a trial shouldn't be treated like entertainment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the rope that broke and caused the water tank to fall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The rope looks pretty durable! How could it be burned through so quickly by fireworks?

choices.text: (So either Lyney didn't realize this was a safety concern...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm? Why are you suddenly so serious, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm just looking at where the rope snapped.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Look, this bit's made from different material!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Most of it was burned away, but there's still a little bit of it left.

choices.text: It seems to be flammable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so if a rope meant to hold something was made with that kind of material in it, then that means...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Paimon should write all this down! Let's take notes!

choices.text: Like a type of flash cotton.

talks.objective: Ask how Lyney's doing on his end

dialogues.speaker: Molly
dialogues.text: Understood, then I will be going with you. Just so you're aware, I will be monitoring your actions and making notes as necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Very good, thanks for being so agreeable. I'd pull a rose out of my hat as a gift for you, if I could.

dialogues.speaker: Molly
dialogues.text: You may spare the pleasantries. I'm just doing my job.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You've arrived. Ah, who's this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Me? I'm Spina di Rosula's guardian angel... If you've got a problem, I've got the firepower.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha, sorry. I got a little carried away there... Call me Navia. I'm a partner of theirs, and will be helping investigate this whole situation.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And these are my companions. Would you mind if they join as well?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Fine by me...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, new helpers? I would be most grateful!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, let's just say we're tagging along... It's not every day that you get to see the secrets behind magic performed on such a large scale!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hehe, I appreciate your kind interest. Come with me, we'll be heading below stage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Below stage?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, a world of secrets is hidden beneath this magic box, prepared specifically for this switcheroo trick.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But before I reveal everything, you should have a look first. Notice anything strange here?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm not trying to be dramatic, remembering the details of a trick will help you understand the methods used to perform it more easily.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh. Weren't there balloons and other decorations here? Where did all that go?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, good eye! That said, you're still far from discovering the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The back of the door isn't the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... "The back"? You mean the inside of the door? What's different about it? Paimon didn't notice anything...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, very good indeed. I thought you might not be able to catch that, given that you were sitting in the first row.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The back of this door was patterned. Those patterns are now gone, replaced by a smooth wooden board.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So if you put two and two together, what do you get?

choices.text: Wait, does that mean...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Haha, exactly! Alright, let's go. I'll tell you how it works as we head down.

choices.text: There's another box inside this one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so there was a passageway under the magic box!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And this passage linked the two boxes together.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha. I knew you'd figure out most of it as soon as you saw this place.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The two magic boxes are positioned right above the two entrances of the tunnel.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: See this flatbed trolley?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The box with the lucky audience member in it would be shuttled over to the other side using the trolley.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: This trolley can raise and lower, and even rotate, ensuring that the box will face in the right direction.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I see, so that's the purpose of the box inside another box!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Precisely. The inner box would descend after the audience member was put inside and be moved along on the trolley, all while the outer box would remain onstage, as if nothing had ever changed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's how you did it!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Once the box was lowered, the trolley would store some energy through this device here, with which it would complete the rest of the steps.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The audience member would only be able to feel some slight movements in the dark, and by the time she walked out, she would already be back onstage.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what about your side of the trick?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right. You were talking that whole time, and you even came out for a moment near the end.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah yes, a phonograph operated by Lynette was used to achieve that effect.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My assistant and I had already scripted our conversation beforehand. When the countdown began, I had already gone to the opposite box via a tunnel using that ladder.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And what about Lynette? Where was she?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: I was in a mezzanine space in the back of the box.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, interesting!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That's how we were able to coordinate Lyney's lines with the assistant... And by the way, I was the one who walked out of the box at the end.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I mean, we are twins. All it takes is a change of clothes and no one can tell who's who, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And that's my favorite part of this trick — only Lynette and I can perform it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's how it all worked. Wow, every detail you revealed was more amazing than the last!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can tell a lot of thought was put into this.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Lynette would briefly walk out of the box and then go back in, jumping into the tunnel and escaping before the box on the trolley could finish ascending.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And then I walk out of the other box in the audience area, and the trick would be complete... the operative word here being "would."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But as you saw, Cowell was in the box, not our audience member — she, on the other hand, mysteriously vanished.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: We really don't know how that happened.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If not for that interlude, this would have been an astonishing trick. I probably never would have figured out how you pulled it off...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And yet, to think that someone was able to use this magic trick to commit a crime.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Could we have a look around? I think we can come up with some more leads.

dialogues.speaker: Molly
dialogues.text: This is the scene of the crime, so Lyney and Lynette are not permitted to stay here. I'll escort them back up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yes, of course, no need to be so strict now. I won't disappear into thin air, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Thanks, everyone. We're counting on you.

talks.objective: Search the underground passage for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do we do, {NICKNAME}? The whole situation is so confusing!

choices.text: I do have some thoughts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good plan. Impossible things don't just happen, we'll get to the truth one way or another!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Just relax. Even if everyone else suspects Lyney and Lynette, at least we will be supporting them from the stands.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides, I doubt Furina understands any more about what happened than we do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Navia. Well, we'll be going then.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Best of luck to you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah finally, you're back! Well? How did your investigation go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: To be honest, you might be disappointed...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: No, no. We're already very grateful that you were willing to help.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well now, don't you all look disappointed? Don't tell me that your investigation came up empty-handed?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That was to be expected, of course. The guilty can never produce proof of their innocence.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #But don't let that stop you, {NICKNAME}. I shall be terribly disappointed should you, my most anticipated foe, concede so easily.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just you wait.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Since both parties are present, I declare that the trial regarding the magic show incident is now in session.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Firstly, in order for the audience to understand the causes and results of the incident, could we please have Mr. Lyney explain the trick?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, of course. I will explain, while Lynette demonstrates onstage. All the necessary items have been prepared.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Lyney clearly reveals the details of the magic trick. Everyone in the audience is stunned.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Thank you, Mr. Lyney. In that case, I take your statement to be that...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: You ran to, and remained hidden within, the magic box in the audience stands once the trick began, and thus could not have committed the crime. Is this correct?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honor.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In that case, I call upon the prosecution — Lady Furina. Do you wish to refute his statement in any way?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Why, of course I do. Allow me to take the first shot and break this case wide open. Mr. Lyney is clearly lying.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: There is no way you could have been in the box the whole time if you were to abduct Halsey and murder Cowell. In fact, I'd say you were hardly in that tunnel at all!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That is simply your hypothesis based on the presumption that I'm guilty.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, is that so? And if I may ask, what did you hear while you were inside your box?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The roaring countdown of the crowd, of course. That's how I kept track of the time and built anticipation for the finale.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And you didn't hear anything else at all? Nothing that might leave an impression of any kind?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No, nothing.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I see, but when the count reached thirty seconds or so, there was a thud — one so loud that I believe practically everyone heard it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, hang on, something's not right here...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (How could Lyney not know about that sound?)

response.speaker: Doubtful Audience Member
response.text: Yeah, I'm sure he could've heard a noise that loud from inside the box.

response.speaker: Suspicious Audience Member
response.text: I was right by the box, and I definitely heard the thud.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look at those scales, could those mean...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They probably represent the Oratrice's stance on the trial.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well then, ladies and gentlemen, allow me to use the words of the magician himself: "You never know what can happen in the blink of an eye." Indeed, it seems his alibi can also collapse in the blink of an eye.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Of course, I have armed myself to do far more than smash your alibi. Confidence cannot go unfounded, and my foundations are rock-solid.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Tell me. Aren't you and Lynette actually from the House of the Hearth?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The House of the Hearth!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They're... Fatui?

response.speaker: Certain Audience Member
response.text: No wonder they did something like this.

response.speaker: Calm Audience Member
response.text: So the serial disappearances were the Fatui's doing. Huh, now it all makes sense.

response.speaker: Rational Audience Member
response.text: I've got a feeling that what happened on stage probably wasn't just an accident.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's irrelevant. Our identities have nothing to do with what happened.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Indeed. Then perhaps you could tell us everything that happened during that one minute.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Your first priority is to prove yourself innocent, after all. I'm sure there is little that needs to be kept secret now... Unless your "script" already has holes in it.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (The outlander is speechless. My, oh my, don't they look flabbergasted! Haha, now comes the infighting and discord, I suppose. This was almost too easy!)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (Aw, good thing I made all those preparations. Seems the all-nighter I pulled last night is really paying off!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Lyney, why didn't you tell us this before!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Lyney and Lynette are Fatui...)

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Order, order. Mr. Lyney, allow me to re-establish the facts. Lady Furina has raised two points...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: First, when the thud was heard in the opera house, you were neither in the box nor the tunnel. Second, you and Ms. Lynette are both members of the House of the Hearth.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Are these claims true?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's no doubt about a magician's ability to con others. Given how Lyney has concealed his identity, this could all have been set up beforehand.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Plus Childe is here in Fontaine along with other House operatives, there must be some scheme at work here.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I've been a victim of such schemes before, and now...)

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Please answer my question, Mr. Lyney.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yes, they're true, Your Honor.

response.speaker: Excited Audience Member
response.text: I knew it!

response.speaker: Optimistic Audience Member
response.text: Well, that's it. We might as well move on to the sentencing already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What should we do now, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Permission to speak, Your Honor.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Granted.

choices.text: My client has withheld some key information.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: In that case, what is your request?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I request a brief adjournment. There are things that must be discussed.

response.speaker: Impatient Audience Member
response.text: Is that really necessary? They're already as good as guilty.

response.speaker: Disappointed Audience Member
response.text: The defendant deceived their own attorneys. What is there left to discuss?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Order, order, I say.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Your request is reasonable and we shall adjourn. This trial will reconvene in one hour.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Heh, so you would stick to Mr. Lyney's defense even after knowing what you do now? You certainly have more professionalism than I thought.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: In that case, my dear audience, let's allow the joy of victory to steep for a little while longer, haha.

choices.text: My defense cannot proceed.
But let's take things step by step.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello there. What are you investigating?

dialogues.speaker: Maurice
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, this location has also been cordoned off because the magic troupe members are currently considered prime suspects. The investigation team is still collecting evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Maurice
dialogues.text: The seats were all booked in advance, so we were able to deduce the missing woman's identity by checking the guest list.

choices.text: Could you tell us who she is?

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: Sure, it's not like this is confidential information. We will publish it later anyway when we petition the public to help us find the missing person.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: Her name is Halsey. She's a painter from Fontaine who's made a bit of a name for herself.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: Apparently, she wasn't a regular at the opera house, but she'd been feeling some pressure with her work lately, which made her decide to come see the magic show.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: The magic troupe members all claim not to know her. We have looked into her social connections. It seems that she has no personal grievances or conflicts of interest with the suspects.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: Simply put, she wasn't related to the magic troupe at all, which matches the features of the previous serial disappearances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Were the victims of the previous cases also chosen at random?

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: That's how it seems to us, in any case. Apart from the fact that they were all young women of around the same age range, there really weren't any other connections between them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Okay then.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for letting us know all this.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: No need to be so formal. If you do happen to see the missing girl, please be sure to contact us.

response.speaker: Maurice
response.text: It is of utmost importance that we get to the bottom of these disappearances.

choices.text: We're Lyney and Lynette's attorneys.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: Sorry, but no one can freely enter or exit the opera house at the moment. If you wish to leave, you must register your identity with us first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, no, we're not leaving... we're representing Lyney and Lynette as attorneys, so we're investigating the case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Were you always guarding this entrance?

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: Yes, after the Chief Justice gave the order, everyone coming in or out must undergo a strict inspection.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: So the missing girl couldn't have left from here — at least not from that point on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about during the show?

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: I doubt there was much opportunity then, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you be so sure, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: Well, because I was in charge of security near the entrance at that time.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: I couldn't see Lyney's performance from here, which was quite a shame... Just my luck.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: But still, I did not abandon my post, and I stayed put no matter how loud the applause was. If someone had so much as even approached the door, I would have noticed it, let alone if they had tried to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: We Melusines are good at that sort of thing, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, it's safe to say the girl couldn't have left through here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, thanks for your help. This'll be useful info!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, we've ascertained the state of the crime scene.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Let's find a place to sort out our findings once Melus returns. It seems to me that there are several things that don't add up here.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Apologies for the wait, Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So what did the Gardes say? Did the criminal escape through the vent?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: They believe the odds of that are very low, since the vent leads to the opera house's basement.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The Gardes have checked the area carefully. No one left through the basement during the performance or after the incident, and no one was found hiding there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the tunnel's become like a "secret chamber," then? Y'know, like the kind you usually see in novels?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It would seem so.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm, the plot thickens... Halsey's disappearance and Cowell's death are both quite inexplicable.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No wonder Furina was so confident in her accusation. All the current evidence points toward Lyney and Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: In other words, the "charges" are very likely to be upheld unless we make some considerable progress.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Charges and then trial... So, if the charges are upheld, they'll announce a sentence?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's right. This is how a trial goes in the opera house — during the proceedings, the Chief Justice and the Oratrice will hear statements from both sides.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Oratrice will too?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's right. This is how Indemnitium is produced.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The statements from both sides, the defenses from attorneys, witness testimonies, and even the audience's emotions will all be projected on the Oratrice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: To put it simply, it's as if the Oratrice has its own will, and is a judge in its own right.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: This also precludes any kind of favoritism on the part of the Chief Justice... Not that this has ever happened anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Once both sides have finished speaking, the Chief Justice will make his final decision. This, too, will be used by the Oratrice as a reference.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then finally, the Oratrice will be consulted by officials. The result it returns is the will of "justice" itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So that machine is the one that actually decides? Paimon thought Neuvillette called the shots!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: In practice, there is very little difference. Both have always come to the same judgment — which is why people have great faith in the Chief Justice.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. The Gardes also asked me to convey that none of us will be allowed to leave this place before the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why!?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Because we've chosen to act as the twins' proxies. That makes us persons related to the case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: They're concerned that we might be colluding with outside parties, or that we might find outside help to disrupt the case...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And even if that were not so, it could prove problematic if we happened to spread key information about the case ahead of time.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: I'm ready to break out at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa! There's no need for that! Paimon thinks they have a point. That said... are they providing food?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Of course, I just hope you don't mind the lack of options. I'm afraid that catering to all tastes is not in the cards, nor is any guarantee of balanced nutrition.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now's not the time to be picky.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: In that case, let's just sort out our findings together here. Pity, I was hoping to take you to try some of Fontaine's famous desserts, too.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I mean, what better way to properly think through our findings than over some tea and sweets?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, breaking out suddenly doesn't seem like such a bad idea after all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just kidding, just kidding... Paimon will still do her best even if there are no snacks!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm? What do you mean "no snacks"? Of course we'll have snacks! If we cannot buy some, then we'll simply make some.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Here? But how?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Understood, Demoiselle. Everyone, please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're carrying a portable stove with you?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Yes. I must be prepared to meet the Demoiselle's baking needs whenever the fancy strikes her.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: I have eggs, sugar, and almonds at the ready.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Good work, you two. Then I'll get to it. Please sit tight for a moment, you'll get to taste my awesome snacks soon enough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These three are quite the interesting group...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Must be a Spina di Rosula thing.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Navia methodically handles the ingredients and pulls fresh macarons out of the oven in short order.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, and Paimon thought it smelled good while it was still in the oven, it's even better now! Paimon can't stop drooling!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From the way you had these two guys carrying all that stuff around, Paimon thought you'd have them do more during the baking process.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you ended up doing the entire thing by yourself... beating the egg whites, grinding almonds, everything.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: I was applauding.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: And I was giving encouraging smiles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, that's not quite what Paimon meant, but okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was just thinking, aren't you worried about getting your fancy dress dirty beating egg whites and baking like this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha! Well, I don't think it's carved in stone anywhere that fancy ladies can only read books, sip tea, ride horses, and play the piano. I just really enjoy making snacks.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate beating egg whites, by the way. It's a real arm workout! You also need to beat them to just the right consistency, or your macarons will crack.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, give these a try, fresh out of the oven! There's three for each of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Only three?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, eating too many sweet treats might send all that sugar to your head. You wouldn't be able to think clearly about the case on a sugar rush, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Tea is ready to be served as well. This is Demoiselle's favorite, strong black tea with a floral fragrance that clears the mind and lifts the spirit.

choices.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: No need for concern. I'm merely doing as I should.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright then, down to business. As Paimon mentioned previously, the tunnel seems to be something of a secret chamber...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: However, we can assume that Lyney and Lynette were not alone within it. Some criminal also occupied its sealed confines.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The magician twins could have committed the crimes, of course, but they lack any logical motive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Why would they do such a thing right when everyone was watching?

choices.text: So apart from the twins...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The flower vase and the thud we heard during the performance could indicate some altercation between Halsey and the criminal in the tunnel.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Resulting in the shattering of the vase, the discarding of her clothes, and her abduction...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Perhaps the criminal thought that since she was chosen from the crowd, she would be too easy to identify if she was still wearing the same clothes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks that makes sense, but the real trouble is...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's no evidence that this "third person" even exists.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: True. None of the clues we've found thus far support the existence of this third person.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But the only people left to consider are both technically victims, whether it's the missing girl, Halsey, or poor Cowell...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, could Halsey have secretly made modifications to the magic props in order to murder Cowell before making her escape?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But she had no way of knowing how the magic trick worked.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's right. And even if she had tampered with the setup, she would need to understand the entire trick to pull it off.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Nor does she have any motive. The Gardes said that she has never had any dealings with the magic troupe's members.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Were we not thorough enough in our search?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the sound of things, this is turning into an impossible case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your macarons are amazing though, Navia. They smell great, they're nice and crisp, and super sweet...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, they are my specialty, after all — and I see you've already had five of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Five? Oh, that can't be right... Paimon only counted three... honest!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Please, don't worry about it. At my age, a few less sweets might actually be a good thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, no, no... Being greedy is one thing, but Paimon knows how to count!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, Paimon knows that if she ate too many, then others wouldn't have enough.

choices.text: It's fine. If you ate them, you ate them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, even you don't believe Paimon!? Oh! ...How could you!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon ate those two extra macarons, then may they turn into stone in her stomach!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, alright, we get it. Well, I suppose one of us might have gotten too engrossed in our chat and eaten them by mistake! No big deal.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Melus, set the stove up again, if you would.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are you doing?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Making sure everyone gets three macarons, of course!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, there's really no need to do that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! We don't wanna trouble you...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: As you wish, Demoiselle.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: I have eggs, sugar, and almonds at the ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, this really is your hobby, huh?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Navia does a second round of baking over the two missing macarons.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: However, the discussion that follows does not yield much progress...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, that's it for snack time. I'm going to have another look around the area.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I don't know what we're looking for yet, but we've still got some time. As attorneys, I suggest the two of you think the case over again.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It would be awkward if you got all tongue-tied on stage during the trial.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Thanks for your help — and for the snacks!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, it was nothing. A small task for the Spina di Rosula. Silver, Melus, it's time to go.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'll be back if I find anything new!

choices.text: Oh, it's fine. Everyone knows how much you love eating.
We're left with two other people: the missing girl and the deceased.
Why don't you take a break as well?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Both parties have returned to their positions. Let us continue the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: When last we left off, Mr. Lyney acknowledged the new evidence presented by Lady Furina as fact. Therefore, Lady Furina may continue stating her reconstruction of the events.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That took long enough. Now then, if everyone would lend me their attention.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: At this stage, let's revisit that scene from Lyney's perspective.

talks.objective: Wait until the trial on the following day (08:00 – 10:00)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, this is awkward. I didn't think the Hydro Archon would dig all that up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #I'm sorry, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Yeah, sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon doesn't know where to start. We trusted you two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We based our entire reasoning on the assumption that you weren't bad guys!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not to set the wrong tone or anything, but Paimon's really mad!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm very sorry. I know you're angry, and reasonably so, but please let me explain.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I know you've clashed with the Fatui several times before. I wouldn't be surprised if just hearing the word is enough to make you upset.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But our organization is very, very large, and the Harbingers have very different personalities and goals.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Right now, we want to save people... as many as we can.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's right. I'm sure we're on the same page when it comes to this nation and the disaster that its people might face.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I knew if it weren't for our respective identities, we could become good friends...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's why I didn't wish to flat-out lie to you, but chose to hide some details instead.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The truth is very important, but being completely transparent about everything would see us spending more effort than we need to.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But how can we know this isn't all just another lie?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Right. So, you be the judge. Heck, if I were you, I fear that I'd even struggle to trust me at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You met a Fatuus who works as a magician, a trickster by trade... all by coincidence, too.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But still, I'm asking you to trust me. I am no criminal... at least, not in this case.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Sorry, please forgive us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you both say that, but...

choices.text: Explain the other issue first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, let's hear your answer first. And no lies, now!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course. I'll answer any question you ask.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We've been trying to find out how the Oratrice operates. We want to know why it has a consciousness? Why can it deliver sentences accurately?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: During our investigations, we learned that the machine's core is beneath it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: From that moment on, Lynette and I have been designing this box-swap trick, with the objective of getting close to the core.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that why you needed a whole minute?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's right. In truth, the audience would take about seventy-five seconds to count down from sixty, while I would only need fifteen to get to the opposite box.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So after jumping into the tunnel, I accessed the opera house basement via the vent and went to investigate the room in which the core is stored.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: That air vent was created during the construction of the tunnel specifically to execute this step.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And what did you find?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, nothing. As soon as I reached that room and was about to investigate, I heard someone's voice.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Which should have been impossible, of course — I was quite certain that I was the only one in the room.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That voice seemed to recognize me and tried to speak to me. I chose to err on the side of caution and retreated the way I came.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: On the way back, I saw the broken vase and the clothes on the ground, but the countdown was almost finished, so there wasn't time to give it any thought.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: After that, the homicide occurred just as you saw.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that explains why you didn't hear the thud...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But why do you want to understand how the Oratrice operates?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Because of that prophecy I told you about, of course. We must know all we can about this nation's secrets in order to deal with that prophesied crisis.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: That's the only way we can save everyone.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So, there you have it, the whole truth. I swear, I didn't hide anything from you this time.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It was never my wish to proceed under this cloud of mistrust either...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But like I said earlier, you can be the judge. If you want to leave because you don't trust the Fatui, there's nothing I can do to stop you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, you decide. Paimon'll follow your lead however you choose.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I believe in the facts.

choices.text: I will defend you from these charges.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Okay. Thank you.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Thanks for giving us a chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The current problem is that the scales are tipped pretty badly against you two...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we wanna refute the Hydro Archon's accusations, we're gonna need a seriously watertight defense.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Actually, we already have the key evidence we need.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The adjournment's almost over. Let's go back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. Oh, Paimon thinks she gets what you mean...

choices.text: I believe that judgment will be dispensed as it should.
Where did you actually go while the trick was being performed?

talks.objective: Continue taking part in the trial

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like a hook tied to the end of a rope. Huh, there's all kinds of odds and ends here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lyney didn't mention this earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Perhaps it was a prop for a different trick? But why would it have been left here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever it is, let's make a note of it first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it! It all comes together if Halsey "disappeared" instead of "being kidnapped"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lynette escaped from the water tank, vanishing gradually and leaving only clothes behind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If there's a similar method where a person could be transformed into water...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Just a moment, please. I do hope you know how preposterous you sound at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: How could a person ever be transformed into water? This is reality we're talking about here, not some magic trick!

choices.text: I request that we examine Cowell's personal effects.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Must we, really? I should think that of anyone, your friend Lyney already knows this truth very well...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Magic tricks are ultimately just illusions and misdirection... but Halsey's disappearance is very real. We're talking about two completely different things.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #Even so... I trust {NICKNAME}'s judgment.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The truth must be out there somewhere. Perhaps some new line of reasoning may open if we try to gather all the focal points that don't make sense.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Since Cowell was the deceased, we haven't placed much attention on him.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But given that we aren't making much progress with the case, it wouldn't hurt to have a look at his belongings, would it?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: *sigh* People really do come up with all sorts of harebrained schemes when at the end of their rope. The way I see it, your suggestion that we broaden the scope of our investigation is nothing but a tactic for stalling the trial.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Nevertheless, I believe that this is a reasonable request on the part of an attorney. Since the trial does indeed appear to be at an impasse, I believe that additional evidence may help us make more progress.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Gardes, please step into the lounge and examine the personal effects of the deceased, Cowell.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, a Garde returns with news.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: We are still examining the items, but we have already made critical progress that we feel must be shared with everyone posthaste.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: We discovered several test tubes of fluid within Cowell's baggage, each labeled separately.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: The notebook in his backpack claims that these fluids are "Water from the Primordial Sea."

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The Primordial Sea...

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: The notes' contents also indicate that Cowell belonged to an organization that sells illegal drugs, and that he had an accomplice.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: The notebook has many entries concerning safe usage of these fluids, in which the keyword "dissolve" appears many times.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: One of these tubes was labeled "Opera Epiclese" along with yesterday's date. It is empty.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: The notes also state that these dissolution properties work exclusively on people from Fontaine. It's likely that Halsey was chosen as some sort of test subject.

response.speaker: Esmond
response.text: As such, we believe that the defense's hypothesis is, in fact, supported by sufficient evidence.

response.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
response.text: You've got to be kidding! People, dissolving into water?

response.speaker: Astonished Audience Member
response.text: Could something so ridiculous actually be true?

response.speaker: Hesitant Audience Member
response.text: Wait a moment, this reminds me of a certain prophecy. But... it's just a coincidence, isn't it?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If people can become water, does that mean that the water tank's real use was as a means to hide water stains? And if Cowell was targeting that girl...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait just a minute... Could that mean...? You two, with me, quick!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Demoiselle, wait! What about your partners?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Let's go, just trust me!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Order, order.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It is undeniable that further examination of the deceased's personal effects has yielded some surprising results, but we cannot yet verify the veracity of these clues.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Still, let us assume that these clues are indeed authentic — albeit with the understanding that Ms. Halsey has yet to be found.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Gardes, please continue examining the items along these lines.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Mr. Lyney, it appears your hypothesis is supported by the evidence, so please continue speaking.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course. Thank you, Your Honor.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If we uphold this hypothesis, I believe that many of this case's seemingly unrelated clues can be connected together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, like the metal hook. That one didn't make sense at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's think about this. Cowell's methods must have something to do with that "Water from the Primordial Sea."

choices.text: We might find something there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! It's Ace Detective Paimon's time to shine again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In the original plan, Cowell would tamper with the water tank rope and the number selector, securing his target.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When the magic box containing Halsey was lowered, the metal hook would retract gradually and pierce the balloon at the top of the box.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When the balloon attached to the box popped, the Water from the Primordial Sea inside it would pour down and dissolve Halsey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Afterward, Cowell would enter the tunnel and break the flower vase to conceal the water inside the tunnel, with the remaining evidence being covered up by the water tank onstage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he encountered something unexpected in the tunnel, and wound up being fatally hit by the same water tank he meant to use to cover his tracks.

dialogues.speaker: Approving Audience Member
dialogues.text: Huh, that does make sense.

dialogues.speaker: Certain Audience Member
dialogues.text: That actually links together a lot of the more confusing pieces of evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Oh dear, what do I do? Even I think they sound convincing now! Have I falsely accused an innocent person? Ugh, what a humiliation...)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Now, it seems like the only point of contention remaining is the exact circumstances that led to Cowell's death.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: His notes mentioned he had an accomplice who could be related to the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: On that note, the Gardes have just contacted me indicating that they uncovered new evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I shall now invite him onstage to share it with us.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Thank you, Your Honor. We were just inspecting the luggage of the other people involved in this case...

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: And we found an identical sample of the Water from the Primordial Sea among Lyney's personal effects!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wh—What!?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That can't be.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe, oh I see! Well, how wonderfully comedic, to have your own counterattack only to come back and wound you!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Does this not clear all doubt?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: My dear citizens, my loyal audience, allow me to present my reasoning and bring this performance to a swift close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... Paimon can't think of anything either. It doesn't look like there's any way around this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, seems using the water as new evidence was too good a move... why did this have to happen now?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I think we've all seen enough now, and we have ample witnesses to my flawless reasoning.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I believe this is indeed the "finale."

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Now then, my good, noble Chief Justice, should we not, in your view move—

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Excuse me, everyone, but I must interject!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Miss, I must ask you not to shout and to respect the ongoing legal proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, don't be hasty. I have a good reason for interrupting, you know. Now, would anyone here like to take a little break from all this debate, and see a little magic?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'll show you an amazing trick, one that can bring a young woman who has "disappeared" back in the flesh, right before our very eyes! Please do the honors Mr. Lyney, if you would be so kind.

dialogues.speaker: Confused Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wh—What in the world is she saying?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No offense, Miss, but miracles like that are beyond my scope as a magician.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Come on now, don't be silly. Magic is all about misdirection, isn't it? It often conceals the truth while presenting a fascinating illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But once everyone believes the illusion, can't magic reveal the truth to them once again?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And wouldn't such a trick be the most marvelous finale to today's performance?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Come on, Lyney and Lynette. Give it another go. Don't worry — Spina di Rosula has made the necessary arrangements on your behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But as the magic-makers and stars of the show, I think I should leave the final performance to you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *click*

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: And voila!
Um... Uh, sorry for the interruption.

dialogues.speaker: Surprised Audience Member
dialogues.text: Wait, isn't that Halsey? So the whole thing about people dissolving wasn't true after all?
To be clear, I'm only here because this person told me that if I testified, the merit of doing so would lessen my sentence...
I was hiding outside this room listening to the proceedings because I was afraid that I would be the one put on trial...
I was just feeling happy that no one had noticed me... and then before I knew it, she caught me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, that'll teach you to underestimate us three.
Where should I begin... *sigh* I'm sorry. I'm the one who killed Cowell, I admit it.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Wh—What? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: Firstly, my name isn't Halsey. It's Liliane, and I'm originally from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: I heard that Lyney's show was going to be a real thriller, but I missed the chance to buy a ticket, so I stole one.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: That's how I make a living, I steal stuff here and there... and I'd never been caught before.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: But I was noticed at the harbor a few days ago, and I barely got away. Lyney was the one who caught me in the act.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, no wonder you look familiar. So you were the thief!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney even mentioned that you were pretty skilled.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: Well, and I thought that would've been the end of it, but then the number selector chose me.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: He even mentioned the Fortress of Meropide. That's a prison, isn't it? So you can imagine how shocked I was — I thought he was onto me for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: So I played along with the show while looking for an opening to flee, but then I got water poured on me for no reason, and then someone jumped into the tunnel to nab me...

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: I wasn't going to take that lying down, so I knocked him out and stuffed him into the box.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: There was nowhere to run from there, though, so I had to change my clothes and hide in a box containing performance costumes.

dialogues.speaker: Liliane
dialogues.text: I slipped out after the first Garde arrived at the scene and continued hiding inside the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can a person even hide in there?

choices.text: If they're a practiced hand at concealment, probably...

response.speaker: Liliane
response.text: But I swear I didn't know that the water tank would fall down. Really, I swear it!

response.speaker: Liliane
response.text: Had I known that, I wouldn't have put him in the magic box! I may be a thief, but I'm no killer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that makes everything pretty clear now, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah. Now it's time to refute the Hydro Archon's previous reasoning.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This time, we need to tell the entire story from Liliane's perspective.)

choices.text: A professional thief could make it work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She knew that she would have to go through Garde inspection if she tried to leave afterward, so she has been trapped in the opera house these last two days.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: She had already become desperately hungry by the time we were chatting over macarons, so she swiped two of them right under our noses. Talk about a sneaky thief!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: At this point, all the events that happened in the tunnel have now come to light!

dialogues.speaker: Canny Audience Member
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's the whole story...

dialogues.speaker: Cheering Audience Member
dialogues.text: Bravo. Bravo!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Now then, Lady Furina, do you wish to speak against the defense's statements?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please answer the question, Lady Furina. Also, if I may add, the trial has not yet ended. As such, I request that the prosecution not leave the room before the proceedings have concluded.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ugh! What, are you reading my mind now!?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *sigh* No, I have no further arguments. I admit defeat. But really, could you at least have left me with some dignity?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, look at that. She's like a deflated balloon now.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If there are no objections, then as the Chief Justice of Fontaine, I shall once again repeat the full sequence of events.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The actual perpetrator of the serial disappearances, Cowell, selected his next victim from the audience reservation list.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: With some modifications to the selector, he could ensure that the pre-selected young woman would be chosen.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: To cover up any evidence while committing the deed, Cowell thought of allowing the water tank to fall, which would conceal the water left behind after the young woman was dissolved.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: He also tampered with the ropes suspending the water tank, using the fireworks at the end of the performance to cause the tank to drop and hide the water marks.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: He poured the Water from the Primordial Sea, into a balloon during the preparation of the magic box and stuck it to the box's lid.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Finally, he passed the prepared hook on a rope through the gap in the magic box's door when bringing the young woman to said box.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: When the magic trick officially began, the box containing the woman was lowered into the tunnel, tightening the hook rope and bursting the balloon containing the Water.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If all had gone to plan, the young woman would be dissolved at this time. However, Liliane was not from Fontaine, and thus fled the box with a loud noise.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Realizing that there was trouble, Cowell entered the tunnel and met Liliane. Thinking that the Waters had not yet taken effect, he decided to proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: However, his opponent was more capable than he thought, and he was overcome, knocked unconscious, and placed into the magic box, and thus became his own final victim.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Liliane, according to her own statements, then changed clothes and hid until the performance ended before hiding in other parts of the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: As for Lyney, he was in the underground structures within the opera house, and was thus ignorant of these happenings.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: From this reconstruction of events, we can conclude that Lyney, the accused, is in fact innocent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hooray, Lyney and Lynette! Amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: While there is much in Lyney and Liliane's conduct that should still be investigated separately...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This case, at least, can be handed over to the Oratrice to make the final decision.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: As such, Lyney and Lynette are officially declared "Not Guilty"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Victory for Ace Detective Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Great work, partners!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Thank you all, thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's not celebrate just yet...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Next, I think we deserve an explanation, Garde Vaughn.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: How did you find the Water from the Primordial Sea in Lyney's baggage?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Right! Your discovery caused me to make a serious mistake, you know! ...Or was that not a discovery, but false evidence that you dared to bring before this court?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I suspect that the accomplice mentioned in Cowell's notes was not Lyney, but you, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'm sure you know what you must do to lessen your sentence.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Speak quickly, unless you want to earn yourself a one-way ticket to coupon-town.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: I—I was just following orders!

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: We were supposed to place blame for the serial disappearances onto Lyney and thus cause suspicion to fall on the Fatui. The higher-ups said that this was the best opportunity to do so.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And now that your plan has fallen through, and the secrets of the Water have been revealed, you have become a liability to said higher-ups, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Therefore, you would be wise to tell everything you know and seek the protection of the Gardes.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Y—Yes! I'll tell you everything I know!

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Our boss discovered that the Water can cause people to dissolve.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: It can also be made into a potion which, when extremely diluted, can cause people to experience unforgettable exhilaration.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: We've been in this business for a while now and have made decent Mora off it. The disappearances were also the boss' idea. I mean, this is the boss we're talking about, the—

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Aaaargh!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Huh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Huh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaa!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He... turned into water.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And now he can no longer talk.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Such ruthlessness. I shouldn't have expected any less of them.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: An outrageous act.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: All present, please submit to inspection immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... we're just going back now?

choices.text: The problem seems to have been solved for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true, but...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, please wait...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I know you may not want to speak to me right now. Maybe you don't even want to look at me...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But still, let me thank you again for defending me to the end, even after you learned that I am a member of the Fatui.

choices.text: I just didn't wish to see anyone be falsely accused.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I guess. But regardless, I'd like the opportunity to set things straight...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I didn't approach you with any ulterior motives or ill-intent. I've spoken to you as myself, just plain "Lyney," this entire time.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As for why I'm a Fatuus, it's because the goals of the House of the Hearth align with those of an orphan like me. That's all.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That was how "Fat{RUBY#[S]Otets}her," who you might know as The Knave, approached recruiting us back then, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Knave? The one who controls the House of the Hearth? She's your "father"?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's right. And since we're here, I was wondering... Would you mind hearing a story? It's about my past.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Back when our parents first died, Lynette and I were left wandering the streets.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: To survive, I took to surreptitiously observing an older street performer who did magic. It took me several days to figure out how he pulled off his amazing tricks.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I took my sister through several streets until we found a crowded corner, and we began to perform magic tricks there.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: To my surprise, we proved to be pretty popular, and we could at least stop worrying about where our next meal would come from for a time. But, I didn't want my sister to remain a street rat together with me forever.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Before long, an aristocrat came to me, and claimed that he wished to take us in after watching my performances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you went from orphans to nobility, just like that?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That was how we felt at first, too... As if fate was on our side, and we could say goodbye to those painful days.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But I gradually discovered that while we were called "foster children," he was really after my talent for magic tricks...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: He would constantly take me to all sorts of banquets to garner attention, which he would then use to expand his social circles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That doesn't seem too bad either... Better than roaming the streets, at any rate...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hehe. It took a while for me to realize just how dark his heart really was.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: After one particular performance at a banquet, I discovered that Lynette was not on the same return vehicle as me.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I waited a long time after we returned home, but she did not come back. I went to that noble's bedroom and asked him about her whereabouts...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The answer he gave me was: "She caught the eye of a most eminent person at the banquet, so I sent her over as a gift. I mean, you'll be able to perform your magic regardless of who your assistant is, yes?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no... So he was gonna...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, but wouldn't Fontaine's laws deal with such people?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As far as outsiders are concerned, this is a relationship akin to "adoption" or "foster care," and they have their ways of escaping the eye of the law.

choices.text: Villains.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I managed to ferret out the location of the mansion of that so-called "eminent person," and hurried through the night... But by the time I leaped over the walls, avoided the guards, and made my way in...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: All I saw was the moonlit ground covered in blood... and The Knave, standing there in the darkness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So she'd already taken care of that guy...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's right. She had rescued my sister before she could come to any harm, and had even discovered several girls hidden in a basement — all of them orphans.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: "Father"... I mean, The Knave, might have seen something in me, and so, she made me an offer...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: "The House of the Hearth welcomes you, for your interests align with ours. Here, none will ever betray you. Indeed, betrayal shall never be permitted here."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I was hesitant to trust her. I mean, I had just been betrayed by nobles.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But she was also quick to destroy the noble who had taken us in at first, giving us back our freedom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how the two of you joined the House of the Hearth.

choices.text: That's all in the past, though.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: She... has her own plans.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: She has gained permission from the Tsaritsa to first use the Gnosis' power once she obtains it. She plans to use it to find a way to break the prophecy and save Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So she believes in that prophecy too?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That's right. The whole House of the Hearth is currently working to combat that crisis.
