response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Today's case has also proven that people from Fontaine can indeed dissolve into some sort of water, thus further supporting the prophecy.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Everyone at Hotel Bouffes d'ete, including The Knave, has their roots in Fontaine. And we will always defend our homeland.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: To us orphans, the only connection we have left to this world, apart from our "family," is our homeland.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So from small deeds like distributing Magic Pockets to huge schemes like stealing a Gnosis, everything is aimed at dealing with that prophecy...

choices.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It's alright, I understand. The only thing I can do is relate all this to you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I just hope you can understand that even as a member of the House, I have never stopped making my own decisions, and that I believe what I'm doing is right.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If you should need anything at all in the future, feel free to find me. I will do my best to help you, as plain "Lyney."

choices.text: I understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... bye, Lyney.

choices.text: Goodbye.
But I still can't completely trust you.
The Knave is after the Gnosis, isn't she?
So what happened after that?
I just wanted to be sure that we're square.
We're not needed here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey there! What was with the disappearing act you pulled right as the trial ended?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Were you looking for us, Navia?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, this whole thing isn't exactly over, is it? I do feel that we're getting closer to solving the serial disappearances case, though. Don't you think so too?

choices.text: Well, I...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm? What's wrong, my dear partner?

choices.text: I was really only trying to defend Lyney.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, are you sure we're the ones who can crack a case that's been cold for decades now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And given that there's new evidence from the trial, there should be a trail of breadcrumbs for the Hydro Archon's people to follow now, right?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I see... Well. I won't lie — I'm a little shocked to hear that from you, but I suppose you are just travelers who have only arrived in Fontaine, after all...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sorry, I might have been too presumptuous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't say that, Navia...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: *sigh* And we were having so much fun investigating with you, too...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It was like having new waters flowing into a stagnant mire, causing new hope to spring forth, and the reflection in the murk to become clearer.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha... Sorry about that, I'm a bit prone to nostalgia. Don't mind me...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wait, shall we have a farewell meal? You know, to commemorate our time as partners?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Do we really need to get that formal? ...Well, guess you really did treat us as partners, huh.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, I just like to have a proper ending to every important memory, that way there are no regrets later.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, it would just be a meal, so it shouldn't take up too much of your time.

choices.text: Well, if you say so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't have to twist Paimon's arm! If Boss Navia's treating, count Paimon in!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wonderful! In that case, why don't we return to the Court of Fontaine and head to the Hotel Debord? I believe we'll make it just in time for dinner.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, let's have our farewell meal!

choices.text: Let's go have that meal, then.
I wasn't necessarily looking into serial disappearances case.
I'm sorry, Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: The investigation team has some new findings. Turns out there's an issue with the random number selector after all.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: See, I told you. What if the machine picked some big guy's seat? You think the murderer would've still made his move then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt, but we're helping Lyney and Lynette with their side of the investigation. What were you saying about the number selector? There's something wrong with it?

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: You're trying to help them? Heh, that'll be a tall order.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Lyney used the machine to pick a random member of the audience during his performance, right? The lucky girl that later disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Well, we thought there might be a serious problem with the machine, so we had it taken away for further inspection.

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: It turns out that the seat number it picked wasn't random at all. The machine picks that same number every time.

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: I'm sure you already know that you have to make a reservation in advance to get a seat, regardless of whether it's a trial or some performance.

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: In other words, Lyney knew who would be sitting where from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that much checks out. Lyney reserved our seats for us, too...

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: Bet you see why I was saying it'd be tough to make a case for Lyney.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, sorry to bother you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, even though it's bad for Lyney's case, Paimon had better write it down.

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: I see that you're investigating the area. Well, it just so happens that I'm interested, too.

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: If you find any new and interesting leads, be sure to share them with me, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't have too many thoughts yet...

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: Hehe, then why don't I tell you my hypothesis first? The way I see it, it all started with that loud thud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The thud? Oh, you mean the sound that happened during the countdown?

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: Yes, exactly. It wasn't terribly loud, but I suspect that most people heard it.

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: It's just that everyone was awaiting the result of Lyney's trick with bated breath, so no one paid it much mind. But now that the incident has happened, the thud has become an important clue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that makes sense. So, what do you make of it?

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: I'm of the opinion that it may have been the sound of Lyney's accomplice — Lynette perhaps — jumping atop the water tank, or something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: And when the pyrotechnics went off, she cut the rope, sending the water tank crashing down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But wasn't the noise we heard too loud for that?

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: Perhaps the balance wasn't right, leading to a particularly rough landing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then wouldn't the water tank have started to swing a bit in that case?

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: That's true. Hmm, I suppose I must reconsider...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that does remind Paimon, though. What was with that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Lyney's still talking to the Gardes. It seems he'll have a lot of explaining to do...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: I think someone will be assigned to monitor us later, but that's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The floor is wet. Please be careful not to slip.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, why would there be water here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it was for a trick?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon knows. It's one of those tricks where you pour water into a jug, and then flip the jug over, only for the water to disappear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And here's a broken vase... Huh. Did the trolley knock it down while moving?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That can't be. The trolley moves along tracks from start to finish. It couldn't have hit the vase at this distance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, let's note this down too and think about it later.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, these are the clothes that the lady chosen from the audience was wearing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Her clothes are here, but she's nowhere to be found...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lyney didn't mention the guest having a wardrobe change.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, and do you really need to do that if you're kidnapping them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is so confusing. Paimon doesn't wanna be a detective anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like a vent.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: It seems someone could fit through here.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm, could this have been the suspect's escape route?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Alone, perhaps. But if they had to pull another person with them, this space would be too narrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there are no other ways in or out of here.

choices.text: Other than those that go through the magic boxes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, you're right! Let Paimon write that down...

choices.text: And Lyney and Lynette were in the two magic boxes.

dialogues.speaker: Esmond
dialogues.text: Go ahead, have a look around. In the end, we're both after the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Special Rope
dialogues.text: (The rope that suspended the water tank was definitely tampered with by someone. This was no accident...)

dialogues.speaker: Quentin
dialogues.text: Lyney's magic tricks were the stuff of legends. But the way he did this crime... *sigh* He should've stuck to doing magic.

dialogues.speaker: Vaughn
dialogues.text: Haha! Look, doing magic tricks is one thing, pulling off a crime is something else entirely. Maybe he was just too full of himself.

dialogues.speaker: Esildor
dialogues.text: Hmm... Could it be that I didn't see it happen?

dialogues.speaker: Maurice
dialogues.text: If you do encounter Ms. Halsey, please contact the Gardes immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Tristane
dialogues.text: My apologies, but access to the venue is restricted at this time. Please register first.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Speaking of that, I think magic shows would be very popular in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I can see that... Hmm, maybe I should try to learn some magic. If I could make things disappear, cleaning my room would be a cinch!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: You need not worry about such things, Demoiselle. That falls under my duties.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Oh, right.

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Dropped Hook Rope
dialogues.text: (You don't know why there is a hook here. It might be a prop for a different trick.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Broken Flower Vase
dialogues.text: (A shattered vase and water... Something happened down here in the tunnel.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Young Lady's Clothes
dialogues.text: (The young woman is gone, but her clothes are here. What does this mean?)

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Tunnel Vent
dialogues.text: (The perpetrator could have left through here, but bringing the young woman with them would have proved tricky...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: As the countdown began, he entered the tunnel.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: When the flatbed trolley passed, he opened the box and got into an altercation with Halsey, which caused the loud thud.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: He did not realize that this sound could be heard by everyone in the opera house, which is why he claimed earlier that he could not hear the sound.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Finally, he used the vase to knock her out, before making her change clothes to prevent others from recognizing her.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: At this time, Cowell arrived in the tunnel, having heard that strange noise, and caught Lyney red-handed.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So Lyney proceeded to knock him out too before stuffing him into that box.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Afterward, Lyney passed the unconscious Halsey to his accomplice through the magic box in the audience stands, before operating the devices such that Cowell's death would be ruled an accident.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And there you have it, that's the truth behind what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Does the defendant's side have any objections to Lady Furina's description of the events?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The key to refuting Lady Furina is the order of events — what Lyney experienced and what he saw...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (According to Lyney, he left via the vent after entering the tunnel. He couldn't have had that altercation with Halsey.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lyney went to the room that contains the Oratrice's core. This is the actual truth.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lyney did not take part in the underground altercation. He only witnessed traces of the aftermath.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! Attention! Ace Detective Paimon has something to say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When the countdown started, Lyney did indeed go into the tunnel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he immediately used a vent to access the opera house basement, which is where the underground core of the Oratrice is stored.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once he reached that area, he heard a voice in what should have been an empty room. Since he felt something was amiss, he returned immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The crime scene had already developed by the time he reached the tunnel again, and in order to complete the magic trick, he did not remain there for any length of time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally, he reached the surface, and that was when the accident happened from his point of view. Therefore, he's innocent!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, Paimon did it! Paimon actually managed to say all that. Wasn't it awesome?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: In other words, you believe that he knew nothing of the incident?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Moreover, I believe my opposition's reasoning is flawed.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? M—My reasoning?

choices.text: The onstage equipment was clearly tampered with in a premeditated fashion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If that's the case, then if Cowell hadn't entered the tunnel, who was the entire setup meant to kill?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Assuming that what you say is true, Lyney only needed to kidnap the young girl to cause a new disappearance case. What would the point of killing someone onstage be?

response.speaker: Approving Audience Member
response.text: Oh, they have a point...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, that's right, you tell them! And that's why they're partners of mine. They've managed to turn things around!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: W—Well. Your denial is very strident, I'll give you that! But what proof do you have to back your claims?

choices.text: Do you happen to remember...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Of course I do. If he had been in the magic box the whole time, how could he have not heard that sound? Why do you ask?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah. You're saying that he wasn't...

choices.text: Your claim has now become my weapon...
Your claim has also become a critical clue...
How you refuted Lyney's alibi initially?
However, you say that Cowell bumped into Lyney by chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure we don't need to give this more thought? Paimon thinks there's something off here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Lyney wasn't in the box or in the tunnel. That's why he didn't hear anything strange during the performance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This means that when the crime happened, Lyney had already entered the basement via the vent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The same clue you used to disprove his alibi has now become the best proof. Hehe, how do ya like that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well played!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Tch... To think you'd use such logic...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: W—Well then! If it wasn't Lyney who committed the crimes, then who was it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The murderer was...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That can't be right. Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, the killer was, in fact, Cowell, the deceased!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe, is that so? How interesting. Let's hear your reasoning, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What I must do next is recreate the truth, what Cowell did, and how he went from would-be perpetrator to victim.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The criminal must have understood the methods behind Lyney's magic trick, and must have been in a position to easily modify the equipment.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leaving aside how he died, Cowell had all the means to commit the crime at his disposal.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The strange noise could likely have been the sound of Cowell and Halsey struggling.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lyney was not in the tunnel for one minute. This would have given time for Cowell to bring Halsey out of the magic box in the audience stands.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But according to the Gardes' testimony, no one entered or left the opera house, so even if he had taken her, there'd be no means of exiting.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Exiting from the box would have been in full view of the audience, pretty much guaranteeing that they would be discovered...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What's wrong, {NICKNAME}? Are you still having trouble figuring things out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where in the world did Halsey go...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe. I see how it is! So this was all just a bluff. And here I thought you had something to show for it, but it seems you're still far from the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Look, since we're at a dead end, why not consider a different track?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Just like the trick as it transpired, the end result must have been utterly different from the magician's initial design.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: If only we knew how Halsey disappeared...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that would be nice, but the tunnel only has three exits, and none of them seem very likely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And it's not like this is a magic trick where you can just make a real, live person disappear. Y'know, like you did from that water tank, Lynette...

choices.text: Magic...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait. Could it have been the water...?)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Excuse my interruption, dear opponents, but do you not see that the crowd is growing impatient? There is no greater sin in this opera house than an awkward delay in the performance.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If the defense is unable to make further effective arguments, we will move on to the next stage of the trial.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hold on a second!

choices.text: Escaping from the water tank...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Lyney did not need to take part in the dissolution of the young woman at all. Indeed, he did leave the scene via the vent.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Having made modifications to the props beforehand, his accomplice Cowell then caused Halsey to vanish using the Water from the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But upon his return, in cruel avarice, Lyney desired sole credit and prepared to do away with his partner-in-crime.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ultimately, he knocked Cowell out, and the tool meant to cover the crime up also became a murder weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Now, as much as I regret having come to such a viciously straightforward conclusion, it does seem that the famed Fatui is quite the cold-blooded and ruthless organization...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Am I right, Mr. Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We've used up all the evidence we collected. There's no way for us to make a rebuttal here.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is this the end of the road?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The strange sound wasn't from a fight, it was Liliane's attempt to break out when she was frightened.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The flower vase was not broken to cover anything up, but was smashed during the struggle between Liliane and Cowell...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Liliane was afraid that she would be recognized if she left, so she changed clothes and hid, biding her time... Just what one might expect of an experienced thief.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaand it's Ace Detective Paimon Time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Having been selected out of the blue, Liliane panicked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Her panic only intensified after she entered the tunnel and had water poured on her head. So she kicked the door open, producing the thud we all heard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hearing the commotion, Cowell leaped into the tunnel, only to discover that Liliane had not dissolved.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He did not know that Liliane was not from Fontaine, but was a thief who'd made her way in by stealing a ticket.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mistakenly believing that the Water from the Primordial Sea needed time to take effect, he tried to force Liliane back into the box.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The two broke the flower vase during the struggle, but Liliane came out on top, knocking Cowell out and putting him in the box.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With no way of escaping, she changed her clothes and hid in the costume trunk until the performance ended.

dialogues.speaker: Examine Damaged Magic Box
dialogues.text: (The broken magic box was left on the scene after the Gardes completed their investigation. Looking at it now, the water tank must've struck it really hard...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine White Line
dialogues.text: (This is where the magic box was struck. If Cowell weren't inside the box at that moment, he might've dodged the falling water tank.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Control Board
dialogues.text: (This should be the control device for the trolley. It seems to be able to operate automatically.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Ladder
dialogues.text: (A ladder is required in order to return to the magic box above.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Tracks
dialogues.text: (High precision is required to complete this magic show, and tracks are perfect for making the trolley stay on its designated course.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Storage Boxes
dialogues.text: (All kinds of props and costumes are haphazardly stuffed inside.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Trolley
dialogues.text: (The trolley is crucial for transporting the magic box to the other side. The culprit must've used this to execute their plan...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Magic Box
dialogues.text: (It looks like an ordinary box, but Lyney somehow moved instantly from the stage to being inside of it... how did he do it?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've checked everything of note here at the performance venue. Hmm. Paimon wonders how Lyney's discussion with the Gardes is going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go see, shall we? Things are getting interesting, huh? We're about to see how magic is made!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems we're just about done investigating down here.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes, let's head back up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, it's time to put our heads together. We've gotta get our defense ready for the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's probably gonna be a long and difficult case... Ugh, there's no point worrying about that now, we just need to prepare!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here, take Paimon's notes. They should help you review the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: While court is adjourned, you meet with Lyney and Lynette backstage in the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The brief adjournment ends, and the nail-biting trial reconvenes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hmm, seems this won't produce a particularly effective rebuttal.)

dialogues.speaker: The Deceased's Identity
dialogues.text: (The deceased's name is Cowell, Lyney's assistant. He would've been able to tamper with the equipment...)

dialogues.speaker: Information About the Missing Lady's Identity
dialogues.text: (Halsey is the missing person and an ordinary audience member... or did she have her own scheme all along?)

dialogues.speaker: Probability of Third Person Being Involved
dialogues.text: (Could there have been a third person involved? Is that really a possibility?)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Sound During the Magic Show
dialogues.text: (The sound we heard may have come from a clash between the missing Halsey and the criminal.)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney's Statement
dialogues.text: (Lyney was not in the tunnel at that moment, which gave our criminal ample time.)

dialogues.speaker: Entrances and Exits to the Opera House
dialogues.text: (No one entered or left the opera house through its entrances, so where would the criminal have wanted to take Halsey?)

dialogues.speaker: The Young Lady's Clothes
dialogues.text: (Halsey's clothing was in the tunnel. So there must have been some fear that she would attract attention...)

dialogues.speaker: Tunnel Vent
dialogues.text: (It would have been tough for both people to fit into that vent. They would likely have bumped into Lyney as well.)

dialogues.speaker: Broken Flower Vase
dialogues.text: (The vase was not broken by chance. It was used to cover important evidence — the water!)

dialogues.speaker: Dropped Hook Rope
dialogues.text: (Now it seems like the hook rope was not meant for another magic trick, but was instead some form of triggering mechanism.)

dialogues.speaker: "Water from the Primordial Sea"
dialogues.text: (The Water from the Primordial Sea should already have been prepped before Halsey entered the magic box.)

dialogues.speaker: Audience-Side Magic Box Structure
dialogues.text: (I remember there was something else within the inner layer of that box...)

dialogues.speaker: Onstage Magic Box Structure
dialogues.text: (Lynette was in the magic box onstage the entire time. Did she have something to do with this?)

dialogues.speaker: Special Rope
dialogues.text: #({M#The rope that held the water tank up was lit by the fireworks and snapped. As such, the focus here is on the water and not the tank.}{F#The rope that strung the water tank up was lit by the fireworks and cut. As such, the focus here is on the water and not the tank.})

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: However, nothing is found on the scene apart from the liquid left behind after Vaughn dissolved.

dialogues.speaker: Gardes Investigation Report
dialogues.text: The Gardes Investigation Report indicates that the fireworks released near the end of the show ignited and burned through the rope suspending the water tank above the stage. This caused the water tank to fall and kill Cowell in the box below.

dialogues.speaker: Gardes Investigation Report
dialogues.text: If Lyney is no longer under suspicion, only the other members of the troupe would have been able to tamper with the props.

dialogues.speaker: The Magic Trick
dialogues.text: Lyney gave a detailed account of how the trick was supposed to work: By using a box inside a box, the idea was for the box containing the audience member to be transported across via a tunnel underneath, and Lyney himself would also use this tunnel to get to the other side.

dialogues.speaker: The Magic Trick
dialogues.text: Having changed her outfit, Lynette and her assistant would take charge of on-stage interactions.

dialogues.speaker: The Young Lady's Clothes
dialogues.text: The clothes belonging to Halsey — the lady who went missing — were found in the tunnel. The reason for this remains unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney's Statement
dialogues.text: Lyney claims that he headed to the chamber containing the Oratrice core upon entering the tunnel and did not witness the crime taking place, and thus did not hear the thud.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney's Statement
dialogues.text: As a member of the magic troupe, Cowell must have known in advance that Lyney would leave, and he may have thusly judged that he had enough time to commit the crime.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Sound During the Magic Show
dialogues.text: During the switching performance, there was an audible thump that many audience members heard.

dialogues.speaker: The Deceased's Identity
dialogues.text: The deceased is one of Lyney's assistants, named Cowell. He was well-trusted by all his colleagues. His job was setting up and inspecting the props, as well as assisting with the show and keeping the crowd engaged.

dialogues.speaker: Dropped Hook Rope
dialogues.text: A rope that has fallen to the ground. A metal hook has been tied to one end of this rope. Its use is unclear.

dialogues.speaker: "Water from the Primordial Sea"
dialogues.text: The liquid the Gardes found in Cowell's luggage seems to have the ability to dissolve Fontainians into water...

dialogues.speaker: Audience-Side Magic Box Structure
dialogues.text: The magic box at the center of the audience stands has 2 layers, and beneath it is an entrance to an underground tunnel. This was how the lucky audience member was meant to have been transported without the audience noticing.

dialogues.speaker: Audience-Side Magic Box Structure
dialogues.text: By cleverly concealing the tools used to commit the murder among the rest, the wool would be pulled over everyone's eyes, and they could be used when the time came without arousing suspicion...
